14:10 Local Time, 12:10 GMT, 17:40 IST: Namibia have secured a comfortable 5-wicket victory to clinch the five-match series 3-2. Their bowlers delivered a clinical performance earlier in the day, setting the tone for a dominant team display. JJ Smit and Jack Brassell led the charge with the ball, claiming four and three wickets respectively to dismantle the opposition batting line-up, restricting them to a paltry total of 128. In response, Namibia’s openers provided a solid start, putting together 40 runs for the first wicket. Louren Steenkamp set the tone with an aggressive knock but fell short of a well-deserved half-century, being run out in the 13th over. With little pressure on the scoreboard, Namibia’s batters played with freedom and confidence. Despite losing a few wickets along the way, they comfortably chased down the target in 21.2 overs.

JJ Smit | Player of the Match: Yeah, it was a good performance from me and a big Brassell this morning. Unlucky to just take one wicket in the powerplay. I think we bowled very well. And then just the return spell, reap the rewards. [At what moment did you start believing?] I actually told Erasmus, yeah, the captain (Tucker) is coming hard. We have to bowl very well now. And yeah, lucky that it went my way. [How do you feel about this bowling performance?] No, I think it was good. Every, all the seamers hit their straps and we are coming in. Trumpy bowled really well. So yeah, happy with that performance and happy the series is done.

Erasmus (2/2): [Where to from now?] Yeah, I guess a little bit of resting. We've got domestic cricket that's obviously always important for us to feed back into. Yeah, and just to service the whole country and make everyone aware of our brand and what we want to create as a culture at the Eagles. And then obviously off to the December qualifier if we happen to be outside the top four in World Cricket League. That's in Nepal in December. So yeah, lots of skills that we want to take there and hopefully qualify to the next round. [A lot of support around the field. It must be a proud moment for you] Yeah, it's, I guess, why you do it is also for them to be inspired and for the next generation to take up cricket and to enjoy. And if you can do that sort of game by game and year by year, then that's a very special feeling for us as a team.

It was a hard-fought series, with both sides having their moments. Ireland started with a win, only for Namibia to fight back and take the lead. The visitors showed resilience to level things up heading into the decider, but today it was Namibia's bowlers who rose to the occasion, setting up a famous series triumph. Ireland were without a few of their regulars, but that takes nothing away from the way Namibia went about their business, showing plenty of character and quality across the five games.
